newsitem.title: USA: Motorist shot, inner city riots in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Motorist shot, inner city riots in Florida.

text.p: Crowds threw rocks, bricks and bottles and set fire to cars and businesses on Thursday after police shot and killed a black motorist during a traffic stop in a predominantly black neighbourhood of St. Petersburg, police said.
"We've got a major riot," a police spokeswoman said. "It started over a few blocks, now it's over many blocks. We've got a lot of people injured ... and many cars damaged."
The incident began after two police officers pulled over a black man for speeding in south St. Petersburg. An altercation ensued and officers fired three or four shots, police said.
WTVT television reported that the car had lurched forward, prompting police to open fire, striking the driver.
The driver died before reaching a local hospital.

Soon afterward, crowds gathered in the area, which has a history of trouble with drug dealers. Violence erupted and rioters threw rocks, cinder blocks and bottles at police, injuring several, witnesses said.
One witness told WHNZ television: "We're tired of this. We are tired of what's happening out there to our brothers."
Dozens of police in full riot gear cordoned off the area as police helicopters flew overhead. "It's not under control," a police dispatcher said.
One police officer was shot in the arm, but there were no reports of any deaths in the rioting.

"She shot him for nothing, nothing," Rachel Wilson, who had witnessed the traffic stop, told St. Petersburg television station WTOG, whose van was attacked by rioters. A private car belonging to one of the station's reporters also was attacked.
Wilson said the man in the car had had his hands in the air when he was shot.
Police were urging residents to stay indoors and not to travel in the area. At least two houses, a grocery store and a florist's shop were reported to be on fire.
Firefighters were unable to reach some of the burning buildings, advancing slowly down the street toward the burning houses under guard by a line of police.
In New Orleans, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the White House had seen some news reports of the disturbances in St. Petersburg.
"We are trying to contact local officials for an assessment of the situation," he told reporters.
